sentences.text: This synthetic document describes the Cu–Pb binary system as calculated with pycalphad from the SGTE dataset CuPb-86Hay-LB.tdb; every figure, table and stated value is generated, and the exact values are kept in a separate truth key.
The highest invariant reaction, L1 → (Cu) + L2, lies at 956.8 °C.
The Cu–Pb system belongs to the 20 binaries of the ORCHID benchmark, chosen to cover diagram types such as miscibility gap, monotectic.
The thermodynamic description is the SGTE collection entry (Hallstedt, 2025), which reproduces the assessment of F.H. Hayes, H.L. Lukas, G. Effenberg, G. Petzow, Z. Metallkd., 77, 749-54(1986).
The calculations use pycalphad 0.11.2 at 1 atm.
For Cu, the liquidus meets the axis at 1084.6 °C.
At 956.8 °C the monotectic L1 → (Cu) + L2 takes place; the L1 phase then contains 22.2 at.%.
The eutectic reaction L → (Cu) + (Pb) is calculated at 326.3 °C, with L at 99.8 at.%.
At 1450 K the integral mixing enthalpy of the liquid has its maximum, 6.81 kJ/mol, at 48.0 at.% Pb.
The calculated enthalpy of formation of HCP_A3 at 298.15 K is 0.42 kJ/mol per mole of atoms.
This document is synthetic and exists only to test extraction tools; its truth key lists every boundary, field, invariant, plotted point, table cell and stated value.
